Gujarat's contribution to modern scientific research

Gujarat has played an important role in the development of Indian scientific institutions, particularly in space science, fundamental physics and plasma research. For preliminary examinations, it is useful to distinguish the scientist's birthplace, the location of the institution, the institution's scientific function and the department or organisation associated with it.

An institution located in Gujarat is not necessarily founded by a Gujarat-born scientist. Likewise, a scientist educated in Gujarat was not necessarily born in the state.

Physical Research Laboratory: PRL

The Physical Research Laboratory (PRL) is located in Ahmedabad. It was established by Vikram Sarabhai in 1947 and formally inaugurated as an institution on 11 November 1947.

PRL's early activities focused on cosmic rays and the upper atmosphere. Its research subsequently expanded into astronomy, planetary sciences and other areas of physics. PRL is an autonomous unit of the Department of Space.

Space Applications Centre: SAC

The Space Applications Centre (SAC) is an important centre of ISRO located in Ahmedabad. It was formed in 1972 by combining earlier units engaged in the applications of space technology.

SAC's work includes the development of satellite-related instruments and applications for communication, navigation and remote sensing.

  • Communication: Satellite systems support services such as broadcasting and telecommunications.
  • Navigation: Space-based systems help determine position and support navigation services.
  • Remote sensing: Satellite observations provide information about the Earth's surface, natural resources and environment.

PRL and SAC are both associated with Ahmedabad and India's space activities, but they have different principal roles: PRL emphasises fundamental scientific research, whereas SAC emphasises space instruments and applications.

Institute for Plasma Research: IPR

The Institute for Plasma Research (IPR) is situated at Bhat, Gandhinagar, Gujarat. It was established in 1986 as an autonomous institute under the Department of Science and Technology (DST).

In 1995, IPR came under the administrative control of the Department of Atomic Energy (DAE). This is an important distinction between the department with which it was originally associated and its later administrative arrangement.

Plasma is a state of matter containing charged particles, including positive ions and electrons. Familiar examples include the ionised gases in certain electric-discharge lamps and the extremely hot matter found in stars. IPR conducts research on plasma science and its applications.

Plasma and a Bose-Einstein condensate are different states of matter. Plasma contains charged particles, whereas a Bose-Einstein condensate can be formed in an extremely cold dilute gas under suitable conditions. IPR's principal identity is plasma research, not the original discovery of Bose-Einstein statistics.

Comparing the 3 institutions

SACAhmedabad1972Satellite instruments and applications; ISRO
IPRGandhinagar1986Plasma research; under DAE since 1995

P. C. Vaidya: A Gujarat-born theoretical physicist

Prahlad Chunnilal Vaidya (1918-2010), commonly known as P. C. Vaidya, was born in Shahpur village in the Junagadh region of Gujarat.

He was a mathematician and theoretical physicist known for work on Einstein's general theory of relativity, particularly a result called the Vaidya metric. His important paper on the gravitational field surrounding a radiating star appeared in 1943.

The basic distinction is that a radiating star emits energy, and Vaidya's work helped describe its surrounding gravitational field mathematically. The detailed equations are not required to identify his contribution.

Vaidya was also associated with mathematics education and helped establish the Gujarat Ganit Mandal in 1963.

Gujarat connection: birthplace, education and institution

  • Vikram Sarabhai: born in Ahmedabad in 1919; founded PRL in 1947.
  • P. C. Vaidya: born in the Junagadh region in 1918; associated with the Vaidya metric, 1943.
  • Venkatraman Ramakrishnan: born in Tamil Nadu; educated in Vadodara; Nobel Prize in Chemistry, 2009.
  • PRL and SAC: located in Ahmedabad; established in 1947 and 1972 respectively.
  • IPR: located in Gandhinagar; established in 1986; under DAE since 1995.

Prelims focus

  • PRL: Ahmedabad, 1947, founded by Vikram Sarabhai.
  • SAC: Ahmedabad, 1972, a centre of ISRO.
  • IPR: Gandhinagar, 1986, plasma research.
  • IPR was initially under DST and came under DAE in 1995.
  • P. C. Vaidya: Gujarat-born physicist associated with the Vaidya metric, 1943.
  • Trap: PRL, SAC and IPR are distinct institutions with different research functions and administrative associations.

C. Vaidya, a Gandhian Physicist Who Laboured in India's Shadows,' The Wire Science, 27 May 2018, sections 'Nurturing years' and 'Building institutions'; Nobel Prize, 'Venkatraman Ramakrishnan: Biographical,' sections on childhood and education in Baroda. Online sources consulted 2 November 2026.]
